Hi Mykola,
  Hope you are doing well. Just sharing my personal exp. for your reference and hope some of them would be help for you.
  Actually I made my first project happen before I leaned PMP or any relevant PM knowledge. I think I’m standing on the side of “learning by doing”.
  When my boss handling the project to me, the most important target for me it to make it successfully delivered, which could then, make my promotion or, at least, make me feel I can do something successful. So all the project management work focus on one single target is “Make the project success.”
   Then, how to make it happen? Things then coming to the classical theory of PM, which is called PM triangle — the Scope, the Time and the Resource (there are many version of PM triangle, more or less the same).
   Scope – is actually what / how many works needs to be done for this project? Usually, in Software / System domain, it’s talking about whether we need to do an APP / Web Portal / Report System or, 2 of them or, all of them? OK, if we confirmed the client need an APP + Web Report System, here we comes to the 2nd step, Breakdown. There is a concept of “WBS” which you can search for more topics about it. Simply, it’s defining whether we need to do an Android App / iOS App or, both. This is the simple breakdown of “APP”. You can do the same breakdown for Web System to details.
   For tools to clearly define WBS, the simplest way is using Excel. Or you can search any tools online. You can make clearly Tree Structure / Category / Subcategory to describe the “Scope”, until to the very detailed tasks, which you can very easily evaluate, how much time / how many resources (developers / designers) you need to complete this task.
   Time / Resource – Let me talk about these 2 together. As when you have more resources, you make it done within less time. So when we do software developing schedule evaluation, we should have some general concept of how “1 Man-day” can do. For example, a normal Android App can be done by 2 developers within 2 months (60 days). But what is “normal” means? Let’s make it more specific, say an App with about 30 pages, can be done by 2 developers within 60 days. Then 1 page of App needs 2*60 / 30 = 4 man-day. This value changes by different kind of technology / system environment. But after years of working with developers, you will know very clearly about how many “man-day” a static / dynamic webpage, or an simple/middle/complicated function modules needs. Then, by evaluate your “WBS” detailed tasks one by one, you put on your evaluation of man-day to reach an overall evaluation of your project. And then you may do micro-adjustment by talking to your boss / someone professional for those parts which you are not so confidence about.
  If, say, the project cost 1000 (3 years) man-day in total, then the resource you need is depends on the deadline request. If the client need your team to make it done in 6 months, then you need 6 developers to do it. Then, we may come to another topic about PM, the Risk – usually, if the boss only give you 5 people to complete the project, there is not too much risk, however if only give you 3, you need to talk and challenge on it.
  Besides the PM triangle, I do 3 of very important things in project management. They are Communication, Follow Up and Documentation.
  Communication – this we can only talk on general level, as communicate to Chinese people here will be quite different from what you will do in your country. The most important thing is, when we say “This project is success”, usually, it’s the “Important Person” of this project say, “I think this project is success”. The “Important Person” is the Stakeholder of PM. You need keep updating the big progress / important changing / successful output of the project to him/her/them. Here we always have “Silent” technical developers working very hard while nobody knows the work have already been done. 2nd, when you need resources, you may impacting other people / project’s schedule, communication skills will always be needed.
   Follow up and documentation is my personal ways of doing projects. To be simply is writing done all the details in a TODO list in Excel, prioritizing them, check them one by one, day by day, to see, whether this is done, this is on-track, that is out-of-control, then I need to talk to the leader / I need to ask for help.
   As I’m doing follow up day by day, usually, leveraging more resources if I found something is not catching the plan, as earlier as possible. I usually made RISK to be controlled before they become a PROBLEM.
   The PM method and skills is a very big topic. As I am not running into detailed software projects now, I may forgot some other key things. Hope this could be help for you or for your further learning.

CONVERSATION TITLE: Strategia marketingowa w praktyce!
CONTENT:
Dzień dobry LinkedIn Member,


ostatnie tygodnie pokazały trudności związane z rozwojem firmy w Polsce. Przedsiębiorstwa nieustannie dążą do optymalizacji zysków i kosztów. Często w tym przypadku patrzą na działania marketingowe, ponieważ można realnie mierzyć ich efektywność, stopę zwrotu i wpływają one na zwiększenie sprzedaży w firmie. Działania marketingowe dobrze działają wyłącznie wtedy, kiedy są dobrze zaplanowane. 


🔴 Badania na temat strategii marketingowej jasno pokazują, że:

  • 54% firm w Polsce deklaruje, że ma strategię marketingową.
  • Aż połowa z nich błędnie definiuje czym jest strategia marketingowa, co może oznaczać, że strategię posiada zaledwie około 25% firm.
  • 79% badanych firm uważa, że strategia wyznacza kierunki działania, a 57% że wskazuje kierunek rozwoju dla organizacji.
  • Wśród respondentów, którzy nie posiadają strategii, aż 77% uważa, że jej wdrożenie miałoby pozytywny impakt na biznes.
  • Tylko 17% firm bada zwrot z inwestycji, co oznacza, że 83% wydaje budżety marketingowe bez wiedzy, czy były one efektywne!

Strategia marketingowa to mapa drogowa dla Twojego biznesu. Jej szczegółowe opracowanie pozwoli Twojej firmie na świadome planowanie, rozwój i realizację celów. Precyzyjne opracowany koncept rozwoju pozwala na efektywne działanie, zabezpieczy Twoją firm na wypadek ewentualnego kryzysu, oszczędzi pieniądze i pomoże rozwijać firmę w przemyślany sposób.


Zapraszamy do udziału w wyjątkowym szkoleniu prowadzonym przez praktyków marketingu i strategii. Podczas niego opowiemy o tym, 



jak budować marketing oparty na faktach, odpowiadający na potrzeby Klienta i jak alokować budżety, by widać było ich zwrot.



Szkolenie prowadzone jest przez strategów marketingu, na żywo, w formule online, w kameralnych grupach. Cały czas masz kontakt z prowadzącymi. Po szkoleniu możliwe są dodatkowe konsultacje indywidualne. Najbliższe terminy szkoleń to:

  • 16-17 grudnia 2021 (zostały 3 miejsca)
  • 20-21 stycznia 2022 (Early Bird)
  • 17-18 lutego 2022 (Early Bird)

 

Już dziś zapisz się na szkolenie i wykorzystaj praktyczną wiedzę w rozwoju swojego biznesu!
